title: Visayas grid under red, yellow alerts on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026
summary: Power interruptions are expected as the Visayas Grid will be placed under red and yellow alert on Monday, November 23, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.

blocks.text: Power interruptions are expected as the Visayas Grid will be placed under red and yellow alert on Monday, November 23, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.
In an advisory, the NGCP said that red alert will take place from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m.
Meanwhile, the yellow alert will take effect from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., and 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.
The red and yellow alert declarations are due to outages in several power plants in the Visayas, the grid operator said.
There will be an unplanned outage of Therma Visayas Inc. (TVI) Unit 2, while the TVI Unit 2 is running on derated capacity.
There is also a planned outage of a Palm Concepcion Power Corporation and KEPCO SPC Power Corporation Unit 2.
Further, power import from Mindanao remained limited due to the unavailability of GNPower Kauswagan Unit 3, STEAG Unit 2, and FDC Unit 3 - which are all on planned outage.

Meanwhile, eight plants are on forced outage in November, one plant since October, two plants since September, two plants since August, one plant since June, three plants since 2025, one plant since 2024, two plants since 2023, and one plant since 2021. There are also 21 plants running on derated capacities, for a total of 612.5MW unavailable to the grid.
A red alert status is issued when power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the transmission grid's regulating requirement.
Meanwhile, a yellow alert is issued when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement.
To address the thinning energy reserves in the Visayas grid, the Department of Energy (DOE) earlierorderedthe NGCP to install over 250 megawatts of battery energy storage system.
The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) also earlier issued 24 show-cause orders (SCO) against 13 power generation companies over power outages that hit the Visayas and Mindanao. — RSJ, GMA News
